COVER_ARTIST.responsibility: Own cover-scale compositions with strong focal contrast, broad scene storytelling, and clear masthead breathing room.
style_rules: Design for a full-page magazine cover, not an insert illustration.
Hold the top third open enough for masthead and cover-line placement.
Favor one dominant scene with secondary supporting details rather than a busy collage of unrelated moments.

EDITORIAL_SCENE_ARTIST.responsibility: Create page-aware narrative scenes that support feature storytelling and leave disciplined overlay space for typography.
style_rules: Stage one coherent editorial moment or environment tied directly to the article summary.
Use period-correct props, lighting, and human activity to imply the story without baking in labels or captions.
Keep the calmest negative space inside the declared title, body, and sidebar zones.

INFOGRAPHIC_ARTIST.responsibility: Build restrained background structures for chart, stat, snapshot, and timeline pages without replacing the real data overlay.
style_rules: Support numeric storytelling with graphic rhythm, framing, and icon-level cues rather than finished charts.
Keep backgrounds quieter and more modular than feature-scene artwork.
Never render legible data labels, axes, tables, or ranking text into the art layer.

COMIC_ARTIST.responsibility: Provide comic-specific artwork support with panel-friendly staging, expressive action, and clean room for page composition.
style_rules: Compose for sequential storytelling and panel rhythm rather than a single poster-like illustration.
Use bold silhouettes and readable action beats that survive downscaling on a magazine page.
Keep speech, captions, and final panel text out of the generated artwork.

SPOT_ARTIST.responsibility: Handle small decorative, utility, and department pages with compact scene motifs that support layout without overwhelming copy.
style_rules: Favor simple props, vignettes, and atmospheric details over large cinematic action.
Keep ornamentation modular so the layout engine can place typography cleanly on top.
Treat the page as editorial support art, not a simulated finished advertisement or magazine spread.
